title: Ship it right
summary: The shipping discipline: spec to deploy, the release tagged and noted, the pager wired, and when something breaks, a blameless postmortem with the follow-ups filed.

parts.title: Ship a feature (spec to deploy)
parts.guidance: Define the feature's user outcome, acceptance criteria and release constraints before implementation. Follow the feature workflow through review, testing and the authorized deployment path, keeping unresolved risks visible. Give the release process the deployed version, user-visible behavior and verification results, including any functionality still waiting for rollout.

parts.title: Cut a release
parts.guidance: Prepare the release from the reviewed changes intended for the selected version. Use the release workflow to verify included commits, notes, artifacts and rollback or recovery arrangements before publication. Preserve the released version and deployment result, keeping customer-facing notes aligned with functionality that has actually reached the target environment.

parts.title: Set up on-call & incident response
parts.guidance: Set up operational coverage for the released system using actionable alerts, clear ownership and tested escalation paths. Follow the incident-management workflow to verify the handoff and response procedure. Test that a production signal reaches the assigned responder, who can access the current runbook and escalate any coverage gap.

parts.title: Run an incident postmortem
parts.guidance: Reconstruct the incident from the timeline, user impact and operational evidence. Have participants correct the sequence and distinguish observed causes from hypotheses. Turn the review into a small set of specific improvements with owners and tracked follow-ups, linking them to the incident so the team can later verify whether the failure mode was addressed.
